PRINTER'S NO. 4002
THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF PENNSYLVANIA
HOUSE BILL
Session of
2829 2026
No.
INTRODUCED BY GUZMAN, HILL-EVANS, BURGOS, D. WILLIAMS AND
SANCHEZ, OCTOBER 5, 2026
REFERRED TO COMMITTEE ON COMMUNICATIONS AND TECHNOLOGY,
OCTOBER 5, 2026
AN ACT
Providing for the establishment of standards, protections and
transparency of artificial intelligence frameworks developed
by frontier developers; imposing duties on the Pennsylvania
Emergency Management Agency and the Attorney General; and
imposing penalties.
The General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
hereby enacts as follows:
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions
Section 101. Short title.
Section 102. Definitions.
Section 103. Scope and applicability.
Section 104. Administration.
Chapter 5. Creation of AI Framework
Section 501. Creation and review.
Section 502. Records of AI framework.
Section 503. Modification.
Section 504. Audit.
Section 505. Assessment of catastrophic risk.

Section 506. Prohibition.
Chapter 7. Reports
Section 701. Transparency.
Section 702. Reporting critical safety incidents.
Section 703. Agency report on critical safety incidents.
Chapter 11. Miscellaneous Provisions
Section 1101. Interoperability.
Section 1102. Confidential information.
Section 1103. Whistleblower protections.
Section 1104. Prohibited misrepresentations.
Section 1105. Civil penalties and remedies.
Section 1106. Duties and obligations.
Section 1107. Commonwealth preemption.
Section 1108. Regulations.
Section 1109. Applicability.
Section 1110. Effective date.
CHAPTER 1
PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS
Section 101. Short title.
This act shall be known and may be cited as the Frontier
Artificial Intelligence Safety, Transparency and Accountability
Act.
Section 102. Definitions.
The following words and phrases when used in this act shall
have the meanings given to them in this section unless the
context clearly indicates otherwise:
"Affiliate." A person controlling, controlled by or under
common control with a specified person, directly or indirectly,
through one or more intermediaries.
"Agency." The Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency.

"Artificial intelligence" or "AI." The term shall have the
same meaning as under 18 Pa.C.S. § 3131(g) (relating to unlawful
dissemination of intimate image).
"Catastrophic risk." As follows:
(1) A foreseeable and material risk that a frontier
developer's development, storage, use or deployment of a
frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or
serious injury to, more than 50 people or more than
$1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss of, property arising
from a single incident involving a frontier model doing any
of the following:
(i) Providing expert-level assistance in the
creation or release of a chemical, biological,
radiological or nuclear weapon.
(ii) Engaging in conduct with no meaningful human
oversight, intervention or supervision that is either a
cyberattack or, if the conduct had been committed by a
human, would constitute the crime of murder, assault,
extortion or theft, including theft by false pretense.
(iii) Evading the control of its frontier developer
or user.
(2) The term does not include a foreseeable and material
risk from any of the following:
(i) Information that a frontier model outputs if the
information is otherwise publicly accessible in a
substantially similar form from a source other than a
foundation model.
(ii) Lawful activity of the Federal Government.
(iii) Harm caused by a frontier model in combination
with other software if the frontier model did not

materially contribute to the harm.
"Covered employee." An employee responsible for assessing,
managing or addressing the risk of critical safety incidents.
"Critical safety incident." Any of the following:
(1) Harm resulting from the materialization of a
catastrophic risk.
(2) A frontier model that uses deceptive techniques
against the frontier developer to subvert the controls or
monitoring of its frontier developer outside of the context
of an evaluation designed to elicit this behavior and in a
manner that demonstrates materially increased catastrophic
risk.
(3) A known incidence of death or bodily injury
resulting from loss of control of a frontier model.
(4) An incident of the following kinds that occurs in a
manner that provides demonstrable evidence of an increased
risk that a frontier model will cause or materially
contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than
50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss
of, property:
(i) A frontier model autonomously engaging in
behavior other than at the request of a user.
(ii) Theft, misappropriation, malicious use,
inadvertent release, unauthorized access to, modification
of, exfiltration of or escape of the model weights of a
frontier model.
(iii) The critical failure of a technical or
administrative control, including a control limiting the
ability to modify a frontier model.
(iv) Unauthorized use of a frontier model.

"Deploy." To make a frontier model available to a third
party for use, modification, copying or combination with other
software. The term does not include making a frontier model
available to a third party for the primary purpose of
researching, developing or evaluating the frontier model.
"Foundation model." An artificial intelligence model that is
all of the following:
(1) Trained on a broad data set.
(2) Designed for generality of output.
(3) Adaptable to a wide range of distinctive tasks.
"Frontier AI framework." Documented technical and
organizational protocols to manage, assess and mitigate
catastrophic risks.
"Frontier developer." A person who trains, or initiates the
training of, a frontier model using computing power that meets
the technical specifications of a frontier model.
"Frontier model." A foundation model that was trained using
a quantity of computing power greater than 10 ^ 26 integer or
floating-point operations. The quantity of computing power
described in this definition shall include computing for the
original training run and for any subsequent fine-tuning,
reinforcement learning or other material modifications the
developer applies to a preceding foundation model.
"Large frontier developer." A frontier developer that,
together with its affiliates, collectively had annual gross
revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar
year.
"Model weight." A numerical parameter in a frontier model
that is adjusted through training and that helps determine how
inputs are transformed into outputs.

"Person." An individual, proprietorship, firm, partnership,
joint venture, syndicate, business trust, company, corporation,
limited liability company, association, committee or any other
nongovernmental organization or group of persons acting in
concert.
"Political subdivision." A county, city, borough,
incorporated town, township, home rule municipality, municipal
authority or other unit of local government in this
Commonwealth.
"Property." Includes both tangible and intangible property.
Section 103. Scope and applicability.
This act shall apply only to frontier models that are
developed, deployed or operating in whole or in part in this
Commonwealth. Nothing in this act:
(1) shall be construed to prohibit lawful research,
development, testing or evaluation of artificial intelligence
models; or
(2) imposes a requirement on a person solely because the
person develops, deploys or operates an artificial
intelligence model that is not a frontier model.
Section 104. Administration.
(a) Duty of agency.--The agency, in consultation with the
Attorney General, the Office of Administration and the Office of
Information Technology, shall administer this act.
(b) Disclosure statement.--
(1) Beginning January 1, 2028, a large frontier
developer may not develop, deploy or operate a frontier
model, in whole or in part in this Commonwealth, without
having a current disclosure statement filed with the agency
and paying the required fee.

(2) The disclosure statement shall be filed in the form
and manner prescribed by the agency on the agency's publicly
accessible Internet website and shall contain all information
required by the agency. The disclosure statement shall be
renewed annually, whenever ownership of the frontier model is
transferred or whenever there is a material change to the
information reported in the previously filed disclosure
statement, whichever occurs earlier.
(3) The disclosure statement shall identify:
(i) The identity of the large frontier developer and
all names under which the large frontier developer
conducts business.
(ii) The address of the principal place of business
and the address of each office the large frontier
developer maintains in this Commonwealth.
(iii) If the large frontier developer or the
ultimate parent of the large frontier developer is a
privately or closely held company, a list of all persons
or entities that beneficially own a 5% or greater
interest in the large frontier developer at the time the
disclosure statement is filed and a list of persons who
formerly beneficially owned a 5% or greater interest in
the large frontier developer or its predecessors in the
preceding five years.
(iv) If the large frontier developer or the ultimate
parent of the large frontier developer is a publicly
traded company, a list of all persons or entities that
beneficially own a 50% or greater interest in the large
frontier developer at the time the disclosure statement
is filed.

(v) The name and contact information of a primary
contact, secondary contact and tertiary contact for the
large frontier developer. The primary contact shall be
responsible for receiving inquiries relating to this act
from the agency or other governmental entities.
(c) Fees.--The agency shall charge and collect fees from
large frontier developers for the expenses of administering this
act, which shall be nonrefundable unless otherwise indicated.
Each large frontier developer shall pay to the agency the large
frontier developer's pro rata share of the cost of
administration of this act, as estimated by the agency, for the
current year and any deficit actually incurred in the
administration of this act in prior years.
(d) Penalties.--If a large frontier developer develops,
deploys or operates a frontier model in this Commonwealth
without a current disclosure filed with the agency as required
by this section, submits false information in its disclosure or
fails to timely pay any assessment required, the agency may,
after notice and hearing, levy civil penalties, fees and costs
as follows:
(1) A civil penalty of $1,000 for each day the large
frontier developer fails to file a disclosure as required by
this section or fails to correct false information.
(2) An amount equal to the assessments owed.
(e) List of large frontier developers.--The agency shall
maintain and publish a list of large frontier developers that
have filed disclosure statements. The list shall not include the
contact information required under subsection (b)(3)(v).
CHAPTER 5
CREATION OF AI FRAMEWORK

Section 501. Creation and review.
(a) Duty of large frontier developer.--Beginning January 1,
2028, a large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply
with and clearly and conspicuously publish on its publicly
accessible Internet website a frontier AI framework that applies
to the large frontier developer's frontier models and describes
how the large frontier developer approaches all of the
following:
(1) Incorporating national standards, international
standards and industry-consensus best practices into its
frontier AI framework.
(2) Defining and assessing thresholds used by the large
frontier developer to identify and assess whether a frontier
model has capabilities that could pose a catastrophic risk,
which may include multiple-tiered thresholds.
(3) Applying mitigations to address the potential for
catastrophic risks based on the results of assessments under
paragraph (2).
(4) Reviewing assessments and adequacy of mitigations as
part of the decision to deploy a frontier model or use it
extensively internally.
(5) Using third parties to assess the potential for
catastrophic risks and the effectiveness of mitigations of
catastrophic risks.
(6) Revisiting and updating the frontier AI framework,
including any criteria that trigger updates and how the large
frontier developer determines when its frontier models are
substantially modified enough to require disclosures under
section 701.
(7) Cybersecurity practices to secure unreleased model

weights from unauthorized modification or transfer by
internal or external parties.
(8) Identifying and responding to critical safety
incidents.
(9) Instituting internal governance practices to ensure
implementation of these processes.
(10) Assessing and managing catastrophic risk resulting
from the internal use of its frontier models, including risks
resulting from a frontier model circumventing oversight
mechanisms.
(11) Implementing appropriate safeguards to prevent an
unreasonable risk that a frontier model will cause or
materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to,
more than 50 people or more than $1,000,000,000 in damage to,
or loss of, property.
(b) Review.--A large frontier developer shall review and, as
appropriate, update the frontier AI framework at least once per
year.
Section 502. Records of AI framework.
(a) Retention.--A large frontier developer shall retain an
unredacted copy of the frontier AI framework, including records
and dates of any updates or revisions, for as long as a frontier
model is deployed plus five years.
(b) Transmission of AI framework.--A large frontier
developer shall transmit to the agency and the Attorney General
a copy of the frontier AI framework published under section 501
with redactions permitted under section 1102, no later than 30
days after the framework is first published and no later than 30
days after publishing a material modification to the framework.
(c) Access by agency.--Upon request, a large frontier

developer shall grant the agency and the Attorney General access
to the frontier AI framework, subject to the redactions
permitted under section 1102.
Section 503. Modification.
If a large frontier developer makes a material modification
to its frontier AI framework, the large frontier developer shall
clearly and conspicuously publish on its publicly accessible
Internet website the modified frontier AI framework and a
justification for that modification within 30 days.
Section 504. Audit.
Beginning January 1, 2028, or 90 days after a developer first
qualifies as a large frontier developer, whichever is later, a
large frontier developer shall annually retain a third party to
perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements
of this section in accordance with the following:
(1) The third party shall conduct audits consistent with
generally accepted auditing standards and best practices and
shall possess demonstrated competence to perform the audit,
including experience employing or contracting with
individuals who possess technical expertise in the safety of
frontier models.
(2) A large frontier developer shall not retain a third
party if either the large frontier developer or the third
party has a financial interest in the other party.
(3) A large frontier developer may compensate a third
party for its services but may not condition any payment or
the amount of any payment on the results of the third party's
audit.
(4) The third party shall be granted access to all
materials reasonably necessary to comply with the third

party's obligations under this subsection, including all
unredacted versions of materials published under this act. To
protect the frontier developer's trade secrets and
confidential business information, cybersecurity, national
security of the United States or public safety, a large
frontier developer may impose security protocols on the third
party, including restrictions on note taking, copying,
retaining or removing materials, requirements for on-premises
review and confidentiality requirements.
(5) The third party shall produce a report that includes
all of the following:
(i) A description of whether the large frontier
developer has substantially complied with the
requirements of this section.
(ii) If applicable, a description of material
deviations from the requirements of this section, an
explanation of any deviation and its rationale and any
recommendations for how the developer can improve its
policies and processes for ensuring compliance with the
requirements of this section.
(iii) A detailed assessment of the large frontier
developer's internal controls, including its designation
and empowerment of senior personnel responsible for
implementation by the large frontier developer, its
employees and its contractors.
(iv) A list of the personnel involved in the audit.
(v) The third party's procedures for managing
conflicts of interest and any conflicts of interest of
any personnel involved in the audit.
(vi) The methodology of the audit and the nature of

the information reviewed by the third party to conduct
the audit.
(vii) The signature of the lead auditor certifying
the results of the audit.
(6) The large frontier developer shall retain an
unredacted copy of the report for as long as a frontier model
is deployed plus five years.
(7) No later than 30 days after receiving the audit
report, the large frontier developer shall conspicuously
publish on its publicly accessible Internet website a highlevel summary of the audit findings and a copy of the third
party's report with appropriate redactions and transmit a
copy of the redacted report to the agency and the Attorney
General.
(8) The large frontier developer shall grant the agency
and the Attorney General access to the third party's report,
with redactions, upon request, subject to section 1102.
(9) A large frontier developer shall record, as and when
reasonably possible, and retain, for as long as a frontier
model is deployed plus five years, information on the
specific tests and test results used in any assessment of the
frontier model required under this section or the large
frontier developer's frontier AI framework that provides
sufficient detail for an independent third-party evaluator to
replicate the testing procedure.
Section 505. Assessment of catastrophic risk.
A large frontier developer shall transmit to the agency a
summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from
internal use of its frontier models every three months or
pursuant to another reasonable schedule specified by the large

frontier developer and communicated in writing to the agency and
the Attorney General, with written updates as appropriate and
agreed upon by the agency.
Section 506. Prohibition.
A large frontier developer may not deploy a frontier model
if, based on the assessments and mitigation required under this
chapter and the large frontier developer's frontier AI
framework, deployment would create an unreasonable risk that the
frontier model will cause or materially contribute to the death
of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people or more than
$1,000,000,000 in damage to, or loss of, property.
CHAPTER 7
REPORTS
Section 701. Transparency.
(a) Report.--Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new
frontier model or a substantially modified version of an
existing frontier model, a frontier developer shall clearly and
conspicuously publish on the frontier developer's publicly
accessible Internet website a transparency report containing all
of the following:
(1) The publicly accessible Internet website of the
frontier developer.
(2) A mechanism that enables an individual to
communicate with the frontier developer.
(3) The release date of the frontier model.
(4) The languages supported by the frontier model.
(5) The modalities of output supported by the frontier
model.
(6) The intended uses of the frontier model.
(7) Any generally applicable restrictions or conditions

on uses of the frontier model.
(b) Content of transparency report.--
(1) Before, or concurrently with, deploying a new
frontier model or a substantially modified version of an
existing frontier model, a large frontier developer shall
include in the transparency report required by subsection (a)
summaries of all of the following:
(i) Assessments of catastrophic risks from the
frontier model conducted under the large frontier
developer's frontier AI framework.
(ii) The results of the assessments under
subparagraph (i).
(iii) The extent to which third-party evaluators
were involved.
(iv) Other steps taken to fulfill the requirements
of the frontier AI framework with respect to the frontier
model.
(2) All summaries required under this subsection shall
be provided in a machine-readable format to facilitate
verification of model claims.
(c) Content as part of a larger document.--A frontier
developer that publishes the information described in subsection
(a) or (b) as part of a larger document, including a system card
or model card, shall be deemed in compliance with the applicable
subsection.
(d) Best industry practices.--A frontier developer is
encouraged, but not required, to make disclosures described in
this section that are consistent with, or superior to, industry
best practices.
Section 702. Reporting critical safety incidents.

(a) Duties of agency.--
(1) The agency, in consultation with the Attorney
General, shall establish a mechanism to be used by a frontier
developer or a member of the public to report a critical
safety incident that includes all of the following:
(i) The date of the critical safety incident.
(ii) The reasons the incident qualifies as a
critical safety incident.
(iii) A short and plain statement describing the
critical safety incident.
(iv) Whether the incident was associated with
internal use of a frontier model.
(2) The agency, in consultation with the Attorney
General, shall establish a mechanism to be used by a large
frontier developer to confidentially submit summaries of any
assessments of the potential for catastrophic risk resulting
from internal use of its frontier models.
(b) Limitation of access to reports.--The agency and the
Attorney General shall take all necessary precautions to limit
access to reports under this section related to internal use of
frontier models to only personnel with a specific need to know
the information and to protect the reports from unauthorized
access. Reports under this section shall not be subject to the
act of February 14, 2008 (P.L.6, No.3), known as the Right-to-
Know Law .
(c) Timing of report.--
(1) A frontier developer shall report, using the
mechanism established under subsection (a), any critical
safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier
models to the agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours

of the frontier developer learning facts sufficient to
establish a reasonable belief that a critical safety incident
has occurred. The disclosure shall include all of the
following:
(i) The date of the critical safety incident.
(ii) The reasons the incident qualifies as a
critical safety incident.
(iii) A short and plain statement describing the
critical safety incident.
(2) If a frontier developer discovers that a critical
safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious
physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose that
incident within 24 hours to an authority, including any law
enforcement agency or public safety agency with jurisdiction,
that is appropriate based on the nature of that incident and
as required by law.
(d) Amendment of report.--A frontier developer that
discovers information about a critical safety incident after
filing the initial report required by this section may file an
amended report.
(e) Foundation models report.--A frontier developer is
encouraged, but not required, to report critical safety
incidents pertaining to foundation models that are not frontier
models.
(f) Review.--
(1) The agency and the Attorney General shall review
critical safety incident reports submitted by frontier
developers and may review reports submitted by members of the
public.
(2) The Attorney General or the agency may transmit

reports of critical safety incidents to the General Assembly,
the Governor, the Federal Government or appropriate
Commonwealth agencies. The Attorney General and the agency
shall strongly consider any risks related to trade secrets,
public safety, cybersecurity of a frontier developer or
national security when transmitting reports.
Section 703. Agency report on critical safety incidents.
(a) Duty of agency.--Beginning January 1, 2029, and annually
thereafter, the agency, in consultation with the Attorney
General, shall produce a report that includes all of the
following:
(1) Anonymized and aggregated information about critical
safety incidents that have been reviewed by the agency or the
Attorney General since the preceding report.
(2) Information that the agency deems relevant to
frontier model safety.
(3) Recommended updates to this act, if any.
(4) Developments relevant to the purposes of this act.
(b) Prohibition.--The agency and the Attorney General may
not include information in a report that would compromise the
trade secrets or cybersecurity of a frontier developer, public
safety or the national security of the United States or that
would be prohibited by Federal or State law.
(c) Transmission.--The agency shall transmit the report
under this section to the General Assembly and the Governor.
CHAPTER 11
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
Section 1101. Interoperability.
(a) Declaration.--A frontier developer that intends to
comply with this act by complying with the requirements of, or

meeting the standards stated by Federal law, regulation or
guidance document designated under subsection (b) shall declare
the frontier developer's intent to do so to the agency by
following the process outlined on the agency's publicly
accessible Internet website.
(b) Process for declaration.--The agency, in consultation
with the Attorney General, shall designate on the agency's
publicly accessible Internet website a declaration process and
one or more Federal laws, regulations or guidance documents that
meet all of the following conditions for purposes of subsection
(a):
(1) The Federal law, regulation or guidance document
imposes or states standards or requirements for critical
safety incident reporting that are substantially equivalent
to, or stricter than, those required by this act.
(2) The Federal law, regulation or guidance document
does not need to require critical safety incident reporting
to this Commonwealth.
(3) The Federal law, regulation or guidance document is
intended to assess, detect or mitigate catastrophic risk in
ways that are substantially equivalent to this act.
(4) For a large frontier developer, the Federal law,
regulation or guidance document requires independent thirdparty audits of its assessment of catastrophic risks and
critical safety incident reporting with requirements that are
substantially equivalent to, or stricter than, those required
by this act.
(c) Compliance.--After a frontier developer has declared
intent under this section, the following apply:
(1) The frontier developer shall be deemed in compliance

only with a requirement of this act that the agency has
specifically determined is substantially equivalent to, or
less stringent than, the corresponding requirement of the
designated Federal law, regulation or guidance document, and
only to the extent that the frontier developer meets the
standards of, or complies with, the requirements imposed or
stated by the designated Federal law, regulation or guidance
document.
(2) The failure by a frontier developer to meet the
standards of, or comply with, the requirements stated by the
Federal law, regulation or guidance document designated under
subsection (b) shall constitute a violation of this act.
(d) Updates.--The agency shall issue updated guidance
documents on the agency's publicly accessible Internet website
if the requirements of subsection (b) are no longer met.
Section 1102. Confidential information.
(a) Redactions.--If a frontier developer publishes a
document to comply with this act, the frontier developer may
make appropriate redactions to the document that are necessary
to protect the frontier developer's trade secrets, the frontier
developer's cybersecurity, public safety or the national
security of the United States or to comply with Federal or State
law.
(b) Justification.--If a frontier developer redacts
information in a document, the frontier developer shall describe
the character and justification of the redaction in any
published version of the document to the extent permitted by the
concerns that justify the redaction and shall retain the
unredacted information for five years.
Section 1103. Whistleblower protections.

(a) Prohibition.--A frontier developer shall not make,
adopt, enforce or enter into a rule, regulation, policy or
contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or
retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing,
information to the agency, Attorney General, a Federal
authority, a person with authority over the covered employee or
another covered employee who has authority to investigate,
discover or correct the reported issue, if the covered employee
has reasonable cause to believe that the information discloses
that:
(1) The frontier developer's activities pose a specific
and substantial danger to the public health or safety
resulting from a catastrophic risk.
(2) The frontier developer has violated this act.
(b) Contract prohibition.--A frontier developer shall not
enter into a contract that prevents a covered employee from
making a disclosure protected under applicable law, including
the act of December 12, 1986 (P.L.1559, No.169), known as the
Whistleblower Law.
(c) Notice to employees.--A frontier developer shall provide
a clear notice to all covered employees of employee's rights and
responsibilities under this section, including by doing one of
the following:
(1) At all times posting and displaying within any
workplace maintained by the frontier developer a notice to
all covered employees of the employee's rights under this
section, ensuring that any new covered employee receives
equivalent notice and ensuring that any covered employee who
works remotely periodically receives an equivalent notice.
(2) At least once each year, providing written notice to

each covered employee of the covered employee's rights under
this section and ensuring that the notice is received and
acknowledged by all covered employees.
(d) Duty of large frontier developer.--
(1) A large frontier developer shall provide a
reasonable internal process through which a covered employee
may anonymously disclose information to the large frontier
developer if the covered employee believes in good faith that
the information indicates that the large frontier developer's
activities present a specific and substantial danger to the
public health or safety resulting from a catastrophic risk or
that the large frontier developer violated this act,
including a monthly update to the person who made the
disclosure regarding the status of the large frontier
developer's investigation of the disclosure and the actions
taken by the large frontier developer in response to the
disclosure.
(2) Except as provided under paragraph (3), the
disclosures and responses of the process required by this
subsection shall be shared with officers and directors of the
large frontier developer at least once each quarter.
(3) If a covered employee has alleged wrongdoing by an
officer or director of the large frontier developer in a
disclosure or response, paragraph (2) shall not apply with
respect to that officer or director.
(e) Applicability.--This section does not impair or limit
the applicability of the Whistleblower Law, including with
respect to the rights of employees who are not covered employees
to report violations of this act.
Section 1104. Prohibited misrepresentations.

(a) Frontier developer.--A frontier developer shall not
knowingly make a false or materially misleading statement or
omission in or regarding a document published, submitted or
transmitted under this act concerning catastrophic risk from its
frontier models or its management of catastrophic risk.
(b) Large frontier developer.--A large frontier developer
shall not knowingly make a false or materially misleading
statement or omission in or regarding a document published,
submitted or transmitted under this act concerning its
implementation of, or compliance with, its frontier AI
framework.
(c) Applicability.--This section shall not apply to a
statement or omission that was made in good faith and was
reasonable under the circumstances.
Section 1105. Civil penalties and remedies.
(a) Civil penalties.--A large frontier developer that fails
to publish, submit or transmit a compliant document required
under this act, makes a statement or omission in violation of
section 1104, fails to implement appropriate safeguards as
required under Chapter 5, deploys a frontier model in violation
of section 506, fails to retain testing information as required
under section 504(9), fails to have a third party perform an
independent audit of compliance as required by section 504,
fails to report a critical safety incident as required by
section 702 or fails to comply with its own frontier AI
framework shall be subject to a civil penalty in an amount
dependent upon the severity of the violation that does not
exceed $1,000,000 for the first violation. For a subsequent
violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per
violation.

(b) Applicability.--
(1) The Attorney General may bring a civil action to
recover a civil penalty under this section and may seek
injunctive or declaratory relief for a violation of this act.
Any civil penalties collected from enforcement of this act
shall be deposited into the General Fund.
(2) The loss of value of equity does not count as damage

Section 1106. Duties and obligations.
The duties and obligations imposed by this act are cumulative
with any other duties or obligations imposed under other law and
shall not be construed to relieve any party from any duties or
obligations imposed under other law and do not limit any rights
or remedies under existing law.
Section 1107. Commonwealth preemption.
The regulation of artificial intelligence frontier models is
an exclusive power and function of the Commonwealth. A political
subdivision may not enact or enforce a law, ordinance,
resolution, rule, regulation or other requirement that
specifically regulates artificial intelligence frontier models.
Section 1108. Regulations.
The agency, in consultation with the Attorney General, may
promulgate regulations necessary to implement and administer
this act.
Section 1109. Applicability.
